# Thirst, water and the well

## In short
- Drink one water every day. The first drink of the day sets your AP back to your maximum. If you skip a day you wake up **Thirsty**; skip another and you wake up **Dehydrated**. A citizen who is still Dehydrated when the night is processed dies.
- Walking also makes you thirsty. Every 11th move in the desert since your last drink, or since midnight, raises your thirst by one stage. If you are already Dehydrated, that move kills you.
- At the well you get 1 free ration per day. A built Pump raises this to 2, or 3 when the town is in chaos. Every ration after the first counts toward the bank anti-abuse limit, and a banished citizen can only take the first one.
- Water constructions add rations to the well. Water Turrets and the Pool use up well water every night, and they switch off if the well cannot cover their full need.

## How it works

### Thirst stages
- There are two thirst statuses:
  - `thirst1` "Thirsty": −5 night-watch defence [1].
  - `thirst2` "Dehydrated!": −10 night-watch defence and a 0.03 night-watch death value [2].
- Each time thirst rises it moves one step: none → `thirst1` → `thirst2` → death by Dehydration. Ghouls are exempt [3].
- Gaining `thirst1` or `thirst2` removes the `hydrated` status. Ghouls cannot receive either thirst status [3].

### What happens each night
1. **Before the attack (status deaths):** a living citizen with `thirst2` who is not a ghoul dies of Dehydration, unless thirst protection applies (see below). This death skips corpse reanimation [4].
2. **Status changes of the new day:** a citizen without `hasdrunk` goes up one thirst stage. Cheat Death (`hsurvive`/`hsurvive3`) and `hsurvive2` with thirst in its immunity list prevent this [4].
3. In the same step, walking distance is set to 0, AP are refilled to max AP minus any AP loan (at least 1), and volatile statuses are cleared [4].

Example timeline: you skip water on day N, so you wake up Thirsty on N+1. You skip again on N+1, so you wake up Dehydrated on N+2. If you are still Dehydrated when the N+2 → N+3 night is processed, you die before the attack.

### Thirst from walking
- Every desert move adds 1 to your walking distance. When it goes above 10, your thirst rises one stage and the counter goes back to 0.
- Effects marked `resetThirstCounter`, which every water drink has, set walking distance back to 0.

### Drinking a water item
Water Ration, Purified Stagnant Water, Water Cooler Bottle and Mystic Potion have one drink action per thirst state [5, 6, 7]:

| Your state | Result |
|---|---|
| Not thirsty, not yet drunk today (`water_tl0`) | You get `hasdrunk`. AP are set to your max AP; you never end up with fewer AP than before. A second point type is also refilled to its maximum. |
| Thirsty, not yet drunk today (`tl1a`) | Same as above, and `thirst1` is removed. |
| Thirsty, already drunk today (`tl1b`) | `thirst1` is removed. No AP. |
| Dehydrated (`tl2`) | `thirst2` becomes `thirst1`. No AP, and no `hasdrunk`. |
| Ghoul | You get a wound. |

Sources for the AP rule: [5].

- **Dehydrated needs two waters:** the first only brings you back to Thirsty. A second drink (`tl1a`) gives the AP and `hasdrunk` that stop thirst rising at the next night [5, 4].
- **Second drink when not thirsty:** the not-thirsty action carries the message "You have already drank once today: the only other use for water today will be to quench your thirst later on." [5].
- **Full AP:** the not-thirsty action also has a points requirement (`fromLimit`, max −1). Requirements with `fromLimit` are measured against your maximum, and the check fails if you are above the bound [8]. So it likely blocks drinking at full AP (see Not verified).
- **Contaminated zones:** every drink action has the contaminated-zone effect. When the town setting `OptFeatureAllPoison` is on, each drink has a 5% chance to infect a citizen who is not already infected. For a Great Plague victim (`tg_infect_wtns`) that becomes 50% [9].

### Water items
- **Water Cooler Bottle (3/2/1 rations):** drinking uses one charge (3 → 2 → 1 → empty). Filling uses one Water Ration to add one charge [7, 10].
- **Hydratone 100mg:** it treats thirst like water but makes you `drugged`, or `addict` if already drugged. It never gives AP or `hasdrunk` [11]:
  - Thirsty: removes `thirst1`.
  - Dehydrated: changes `thirst2` to `thirst1`.
- **Full Jerrycan** [12]:
  - *In town, no Water Purifier, with Micropur:* 75% chance of 2 Water Rations, 25% chance of 3.
  - *Outside, with Micropur:* 1 AP for 1 Water Ration.
  - *Pour into the well with the Water Purifier (no Filter):* +2 (40%), +3 (35%) or +4 (25%).
  - *Pour with the Water Filter:* +3 (5%), +4 (15%), +5/+6/+7 (20% each), +8 (15%) or +9 (5%).
  - Pouring is not possible while banished.
- **Stagnant Water Can:** cleaning it with Micropur gives Purified Stagnant Water (in town only if neither Purifier nor Filter is built). With the Purifier you can pour it into the well for +2 [13].

### The well
- **Starting fill:** a random amount between `DefaultWellFillMin` and `DefaultWellFillMax` [14]. That is 90–180 by default [15].
- **Taking water** [16]:
  - You may take 1 ration per day. The Pump (`small_water_#00`) adds +1, or +2 when the town is in chaos.
  - The limit is checked against your daily Well counter; daily counters are cleared at night.
  - You cannot take more than the well holds.
  - A banished citizen who has already taken one ration is refused.
  - Each ration after your first of the day goes through the bank anti-abuse check and increases your bank-abuse count. If the check refuses, you get the bank-limit error.
  - Each ration becomes a `water_#00` item and lowers the well by 1. Extra rations show the warning "Don't be greedy...".
- **Putting water in** [17]:
  - Only possible once the Pump is built.
  - Uses the first non-poisoned item found, in this order: Water Ration, Water Cooler Bottle with 1, 2 or 3 rations, Mystic Potion.
  - Adds +1 to the well. A bottle loses one charge; any other item is removed.
- **Devastated town:** each night the well loses rand(20,40) rations, never more than it holds [4].

### Constructions that add water (one time, on completion)
[18]

| Construction | Rations added |
|---|---|
| Pump (`small_water_#00`) | +15 |
| Hydraulic Network | +5 |
| Water Catcher (temporary, can be rebuilt daily) | +2 |
| Drilling Rig | +50 |
| Eden Project | +50 |
| Divining Rocket | +60 |
| Mechanical Pump | +75 |
| No Holes Barred | +100 |
| Divining Rods | +100 |

Building names come from their cards [19, 20, 21].

**Pump daily upgrades:** each upgrade adds water to the well, by level reached: L1 +20, L2 +20, L3 +30, L4 +30, L5 +40 [22, 19].

### Constructions that use water (every night)
[23]
- **Water Turrets (`item_tube_#00`):** uses 0, 2, 4, 6, 9 or 12 rations at level 0–5. It is processed after the day change, before the attack. Its defence multiplier by level is ×0.8, 1.6, 2.4, 3.6 or 4.8 of base defence [22]. The card shows this as 70 base defence growing to 406 at level 5 [24].
- **Pool:** uses 1 ration per night before day 11, 3 from day 11, 6 from day 21, 12 from day 26 and 18 from day 30. It is processed after the attack.
- **Order and shutdown:** Water Turrets are paid first, then the Pool. A building runs only if the water left in the well covers its full need; otherwise it is disabled for that night [25, 26].

## What changes it
- **Ghoul role:** becoming a ghoul removes both thirst statuses and resets walking distance; ghouls never get thirsty [3]. Drinking water gives a ghoul a wound [5].
- **Cheat Death hero skill (226 hero days):** protects against thirst, infection, addiction and hunger for one night [27]. With `hsurvive` you skip the status deaths entirely and your thirst does not rise. `hsurvive3` protects against thirst and infection. `hsurvive2` uses the hero immunity list, taken from the giver if the power was gifted [4].
- **Survivalist's Survival Book, "Water" action:** needs you to be outside, more than 3 km from town, and not to have used the book today [28].
  - Success chance: 100% before day 5, 85% from day 5, 80% from day 10, 70% from day 13, 60% from day 15, 50% from day 20. In a devastated town it is 20 points lower, minimum 10%.
  - On success it resets walking distance. A ghoul gets a wound. Otherwise it works like a drink: Dehydrated → Thirsty, or it removes Thirsty.
  - If you had not drunk yet today, you get `hasdrunk`, AP are raised to 6 if below 6, and SP are refilled up to your max SP bonus [29].
- **Pump:** gives the extra well ration(s) and allows putting water into the well [16, 17].
- **Water Purifier / Water Filter:** let you pour Jerrycans and stagnant water into the well (amounts above) [12, 30].
- **Faucet:** once built, water weapons are refilled for free with water the filtration would waste, so they no longer use Water Rations [31, 32].
- **Banishment:** you only get the first ration of the day. You cannot pour Jerrycans or stagnant water into the well. Jerrycan and stagnant-water cleaning use separate banished actions [16, 12].
- **Chaos:** the Pump bonus becomes +2 instead of +1 [16].
- **Settings:**
  - *Strange soil* (`OptModifierStrangeSoil`): every ration taken from the well gets the "Strange" poison type [16].
  - *All poison* (`OptFeatureAllPoison`): turns on the 5% infection chance when drinking [9].
  - *Well size* (`well.min` / `well.max`): sets the starting fill [15].

## Town types
- **Default:** the well starts with 90–180 rations [15].
- **Small and remote (Distant Region):** they do not change the well settings [33, 34].
- **Pandemonium (panda):** the well starts with 60–90 rations [35]. Constructions cost more resources; for example, Water Turrets need 75 Water Rations instead of 25 [24].
- **Custom:** the "normal" well preset copies default (90/180) and the "low" preset copies the hard type (60/90). Values are clamped to at least 0, with min ≤ max.

## Related
- **Bank anti-abuse:** extra well rations count toward it [36].
- **AP regeneration at night**, and the eating counterpart `haseaten`.
- **Camping and night watch:** thirst lowers night-watch defence and adds death risk [2].
- **Shaman's Mystic Potion:** it is both an immunity potion and a water source [37].
- **Ghoul hunger.**

## Not verified
- I could not read the definitions of `drink_tl0a`/`drink_tl0b`/`drink_mesg`/`drink_hide`. That they mean "not thirsty, not dehydrated, not yet drunk today" is inferred from their names, messages and sibling actions.
- `pointType=4` (the second refill in the drink effect) is very likely SP, but I could not read the PointType enum.
- I assumed the "not_thirsty" points requirement checks AP, which would block drinking at full AP when not thirsty. Its point type is not shown on the cards.
- What the "Strange" poison type does to the drinker was not checked.
- The Water Turrets defence values on the card (×1.8 … ×5.8, up to 406) count the 70 base defence plus the multipliers in the code. I did not trace the defence calculation itself.
